messages.author: 0cb5e1bafbfd5359
messages.subject: Spatial correlation in river networks
parts:
Hello
 I am new with R-inla and I would like to use it to account for spatial correlations in solute concentrations along a river network. 
Is there any way to define a good spatial field for river networks modelling? Have I got to use a particular type of barrier models? Some suggestion or reference?
Thank you very much

Stefano

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial correlation in river networks
parts:
I know river networks has been done using the barrier model, which is
now reimplemented in the add-on package

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/INLAspacetime/index.html

so it runs with the 'correct speed'.

Better though, are the new SPDE models on network by Prof David Bolin
(KAUST) and his group, also available as an add-on pacakge

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/MetricGraph/index.html


I know they are working towards to include time, as well, but you have
to ask them about progress.

Havard

messages.author: 2a6271869edfdebb
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial correlation in river networks
parts:
Yes, see 

https://davidbolin.github.io/MetricGraph/

for tutorials on how to set up such models and estimate them via inla or inlabru. 

So far, only spatial models are available, but these can be used to define separable space-time models in the standard way in inla. More realistic space-time models are coming "soon". 

-David
